evidence.title: FRA-Mainz
evidence.excerpt: Green Mountain's current FRA-Mainz project page calls the three-building, 54 MW power-capacity data center under construction near Frankfurt and reports a Q3 2023 construction start.

metadata.content_hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact 134900-byte content-decoded official HTML response body
metadata.status_wording_as_reported: New sustainable data center under construction near Frankfurt.
metadata.physical_status_scope: The live exact-project page explicitly labels FRA-Mainz under construction. The Q3 2023 start is historical context; the current page supports a generic under-construction observation on the 2026-07-21 response date without a narrower substage.
metadata.currentness_scope: The project remains explicitly classified under construction on the current operator page. The Q4 2026 service date is a forecast and is not completion, commissioning, energization, or operation evidence.
metadata.capacity_scope: The page repeatedly describes a 54 MW site and labels 54 MW as Power Capacity. It is normalized once as planned gross facility power, not critical IT load. The parenthetical 80 MW in 2026 lacks a distinct project or stage basis and is retained only as reported metadata.
metadata.capacity_guardrail: The 54 MW and parenthetical 80 MW figures are not added. Neither is current load, installed or energized capacity, grid draw, generation, consumption, annual energy, or measured energy use. The separate 60 MW future waste-heat figure is thermal output and is not electrical capacity.
metadata.efficiency_guardrail: The page gives no measured or design PUE or WUE for FRA-Mainz. Renewable-power, river-cooling, district-heat, gas-backup, and low-emission language creates no measured efficiency, current energy mix, current generation, current consumption, or avoided-emissions observation.
metadata.role_scope: The page says Green Mountain and German power company KMW formed a joint venture to build the site, supporting developer roles for both. The fully contracted hyperscale client is unnamed and creates no tenant, customer, or user identity.
metadata.workload_guardrail: Hyperscale-client and recruiting language creates no workload, installed hardware, accelerator, model, tenant identity, current use, occupancy, or utilization row.
metadata.identity_guardrail: FRA-Mainz is one three-building project near Frankfurt. The three buildings are not emitted as separate unidentified projects, and the site is not merged with another Frankfurt or Mainz data center.
metadata.rights_scope: Compact factual extraction from an all-rights-reserved operator project page; the page and publisher media are not redistributed.
metadata.capture_guardrail: The response body, raw headers, and curl writeout are hash-bound but are not retained in the repository artifact.
metadata.imagery_guardrail: Publisher images, satellite imagery, aerial imagery, computer vision, and analyst geolocation do not contribute to identity, locality, lifecycle, capacity, role, or classification.
